Verified by reading the actual file content that all 6 findings' buggy code patterns are present at b0e5fb15, so a single commit was used for the whole corpus instead of mixing two.

protocols.added_by: fresh validation exercise (2026-08-17), not part of MEJORAS3.md's own roadmap - built to answer "can MIESC find findings from a real report it has never seen" on a protocol not already in any corpus
protocols.dependency_note: src/ (49 files) has zero vendor/package imports - fully self-contained, no lib/ vendoring needed for this one, unlike y2k-finance
protocols.measured_result: Isolated run (--layers 1,7, this protocol only): precision 25.0%, recall 16.7%, F1 20.0%, TP/FP/FN 1/3/5. The 1 nominal TP (BaseAuth.sol, denial_of_service, matching M-03) was checked by hand, not taken at face value: it comes from threat_model's generic 'external function without authentication' STRIDE template, not from anything that read or understood the real bug (recoverSapientSignature returning a hardcoded constant instead of the real image hash). Same file, same category, coincidental, not a real detection of the root cause - the honest read is closer to 0/6 genuine detections on findings MIESC had never seen before. All 3 access_control/front_running findings (signature/session logic bugs) were missed outright; this protocol's bugs are almost entirely multi-step signature/session-flow logic, a harder class than the vault/oracle bugs the other 2 protocols are mostly made of.

_meta.note: Ground truth = real HIGH/MEDIUM findings from complete, verified audit reports (sequential finding IDs, no gaps), not curated subsets. Categories include MODERN_CATEGORIES (business_logic, oracle, rounding, fee_on_transfer, erc4626) alongside SmartBugs categories.
